cues.feature: playout: the station ident; the desk outputs from its first moment

cues.text: Good afternoon and welcome to The Blether on Kettle FM. Today's question: are they among us? We've got UFOs, we've got Nessie, and we've got cows. Trust me on the cows.
cues.feature: the presenter over a ducked bed

cues.text: Joining me from a caravan site at Drumnadrochit, the chair of the Loch Ness and Lesser Lochs Phenomena Society, Gregor Stewart. Gregor, can you hear me?
Loud and clear, Eilidh. Apologies if the signal drops. The caravan is on a slope and I think it's moving.
cues.feature: a browser guest joins; his own mix-minus

cues.text: Gregor, the big question first. Have you seen her?
Seven times. Twice from the shore, once from a pedalo, and four times in the reflection of a kettle, which the society counts as half a sighting each.
So, five sightings.
cues.feature: cross-talk: both speak at once; tests echo and the mix-minus

cues.text: Five sightings, yes, and a very shiny kettle.
Now, you've got a theory about stone circles.
I do. Callanish, the Ring of Brodgar, all of them. They're landing pads, Eilidh. Ancient ones. And crop circles? Crop circles are just the parking tickets.
Parking tickets.
You leave your saucer in a field in Wiltshire for more than two hours, you get a very intricate fine.
On that note, here's something that cannot possibly be human. Isaac Blues.
cues.feature: a cart fired on its key
playout: a record from the cart wall; the room stays live under it

cues.text: Isaac Blues. Gregor, you were humming along the whole way through. I could hear you.
cues.feature: the guest heard in the room while the record plays, not on air

cues.text: That wasn't me. That was the caravan.
Right, the phones are busy. Let's go to line one.
cues.feature: the presenter takes the call the screener has ready

cues.text: Dougal, you're on after Eilidh finishes this link. Keep it clean, love, and turn your radio down.
cues.feature: the screener talks to the caller only, under the record: never on air

cues.text: Aye, it's off. I'll have to keep my voice down, mind. She's in the kitchen.
cues.feature: the caller answers the screener, still off air
the screener sends Dougal to the desk; the presenter opens his slot

cues.text: Dougal Thomson, you're on The Blether.
Hiya, Eilidh. I'm going to come straight out with it. I think my wife is an alien.
Right. Okay. What makes you say that?

She hums at the microwave, and the microwave hums back. She ate a Tunnock's teacake last night with the foil still on. And she's started sleeping on the ceiling. Well, near the ceiling. On top of the wardrobe. I'm not making this shit up, Eilidh.
cues.feature: a profanity on air: the producer presses Dump within the 8 second delay
the profanity delay dumped; listeners lose about 8 seconds, the room is untouched

cues.text: Dougal, language, please, it's the afternoon. Have you tried just asking her?
I did. She said, don't be daft, Dougal. Which is exactly what an alien would say.
Classic deflection. Textbook.
cues.feature: a second voice joins the caller's line: the guest hears the caller in his own mix

cues.text: Dougal, here's my advice. Be very, very nice to her. If she is an alien, you want to be on the right side of the invasion. And if she isn't, you're still married, so be nice anyway. This one's for you.

cues.feature: playout: the request

cues.text: Seamus, you're next. Keep it short, she's got the news at the top of the hour.
cues.feature: the screener and the second caller, off air

cues.text: Grand, grand. I'll be quick.

cues.feature: Seamus's slot opens after the record

cues.text: Seamus Boyd, calling from near Ballymena. Seamus, what's happening on your farm?
Well, Eilidh, I keep Highland cows. Twelve of them. And every morning, every single morning, they're standing in a perfect circle. Facing outwards.
Facing outwards.
Facing outwards. And the grass in the middle is flattened in the shape of a bigger cow.
That's the stone circle connection right there. Bovine geometry. They're marking a landing site.
Or, and hear me out, they're keeping warm.
Facing outwards, Eilidh? No. They're guarding something.
Seamus, if anything lands, you phone us first. It's coming up to two o'clock. Here's the news with Isla Campbell.
cues.feature: the hard post at 14:00, back-timed
playout: the news sting on F2

cues.text: Kettle FM news at two. Police in Inverness have asked a man who has reported the Loch Ness Monster four times this week to stop phoning them, and to phone Kettle FM instead.
cues.feature: playout: a scheduled element, the newsreader

cues.text: And the weather. Clear skies tonight across the Highlands, ideal for spotting satellites, planets, and anything else that may be watching. Cows are advised to stay indoors.

cues.feature: playout stops: strips say OPEN, the lamp says PLAYOUT DOWN, listeners hear the fallback; the room keeps talking

cues.text: Gregor, I've just lost the news feed on my screen.
cues.feature: the room stays live while playout is down

cues.text: Don't panic. But that is exactly how it starts.
We're on the fallback, folks, bear with us. And, we're back.
cues.feature: Restart playout: ON AIR returns when listeners hear the programme
playout restarted with Ctrl+R

cues.text: Waiting in the wings for Steeped at five past, broadcasting from Newcastle, Finlay Grant. Finlay, you're in the room.
cues.feature: the overlap handover: the remote DJ joins before his slot

cues.text: Howay, Eilidh! I've been listening in. For the record, the only thing in the sky over Newcastle tonight is a seagull with a chip.
cues.feature: the remote DJ talks over the overlap window

cues.text: Finlay, it's all yours. Gregor, thank you, mind the slope. I'm Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod, and this was The Blether.

cues.feature: one action passes the programme to Finlay; the presenter's slot leaves the stage

cues.text: Cheers, Eilidh. This is Steeped on Kettle FM, and we start loud. From Woodstock ninety-nine, this is Bush.
